survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This document is a country note describing governance arrangements in France’s adult skills system; it does not analyze student microdata from an ILSA (e.g., PISA/TIMSS/PIAAC) and therefore does not define a sampling frame, analytic sample, or survey-weight variables. No plausible values (PV) or achievement scaling are estimated from assessment responses, so there is no need for PV-combining or complex-survey variance estimation. For any future empirical work using OECD/IEA-style microdata, analysts should apply the official sampling weights provided in the dataset (and replicate weights if available) to account for stratification and clustering in the original survey design. In this note, the “data preparation” is conceptual/administrative (mapping responsibilities across governance levels), not statistical weighting.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: Plausible values are not applicable because this is not an assessment-scoring study using cognitive test items (e.g., PISA/TIMSS/PIAAC) and does not model achievement outcomes from PV-based scales. The note synthesizes governance roles and responsibilities using administrative/desk information rather than student response data, so there is no missing-item or missing-response handling strategy to report. As a result, both PV handling and missing-data handling are outside the scope of the document’s methodology.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: Used a desk-based country note approach to describe France’s adult skills system governance. No student-level assessment dataset is analyzed, and no analytic subsample is defined.

data.outcome_summary: This OECD country note provides an overview of how France’s adult skills system is governed across national, regional, and local levels. It describes which ministries and agencies set strategic frameworks, design and implement vocational education and training (VET), higher VET (HVET), continued education and training (CET), adult education (AE), and active labour market policies (ALMPs). It also details the roles of regional councils (18 regions), local municipalities (34 955), and local missions (Missions locales), alongside social partners and skills operators (OPCOs). The note reports governance structure and responsibility allocation (e.g., strategy, intelligence, implementation, funding, delivery) rather than student achievement outcomes, and it does not include assessment administration, sampling, scaling, or benchmark performance metrics. Consequently, there are no ML models, PVs, or statistical performance indicators reported.
data.null_fields_interpretation: This is a non-empirical governance description within an OECD review of adult skills systems, so there is no student sample, no ILSA assessment cycle, and no statistical modeling pipeline to extract. Fields related to PV handling, missing data handling, ML techniques, and predictive performance are therefore structurally absent by design. The document’s “results” are descriptive mappings of institutional responsibilities rather than quantitative effects on measured outcomes.
